newsitem.title: CHINA: Ka Wah hit by profit-taking after results.
newsitem.headline: Ka Wah hit by profit-taking after results.

text.p: Shares in Ka Wah Bank came under pressure on Tuesday as investors took profits a day after the company announced its interim results, brokers said.
Ka Wah stock fell HK$0.10 to HK$8.65 in late afternoon after having trading as high as HK$9.10 at the start of Tuesday's morning session.

The bank reported on Monday a 50.54 percent increase in net profit in the first half of 1997 compared with the year-ago period. However, brokers said Ka Wah's performance had already been priced into the shares.
Ka Wah shares started a rally in May, when they stood around HK$3.00 each.
"The expectation is over," said Louis Tse, executive director at Standard Capital Brokerage, who expects the shares to consolidate around HK$8.00.
Tse said a good deal of Ka Wah's reported profit came from what are likely to be non-recurring items.
In addition, some market players expressed disappointment that the bank did not announce restructuring plans as many had expected.
